Uber shifted from pure asset-light AV aggregation to committing >$10B across AV commercialization (~$2.5B direct AV/EV equity stakes including $500M Lucid and ~$500M Nuro; ~$7.5B future fleet procurement milestones covering >120,000 vehicles, anchored by 35,000+ Lucid/Nuro robotaxis and a 50,000 sq ft Houston depot). Separately, Uber's Delivery Hero tender offer secured 66.56% acceptance in Nov 2026 (additional acceptance through Nov 24; H2 2027 close) while an Uber loan backing SSW Partners' 14-market carve-out triggered EC (DG COMP), Korea FTC (KFTC), and MENA antitrust scrutiny.

Chapter 6 and Chapter 5 book/audiobook narratives retained stale FY2025 balance-sheet and buyback figures ($7.1B cash, $10.52B LT debt, <0.5x net leverage, >3x buybacks/SBC, 'never has to pause buybacks') that contradicted Q3 2026 10-Q reality ($15,664M LT debt up +49%, $10,068M unrestricted cash separate from $11,372M restricted insurance collateral, 2.65x 9M buybacks/SBC, ~$1.5B Q4 2026 UK VAT FCF headwind flagged by CFO Balaji Krishnamurthy, Uber-backed SSW Partners carve-out loan, and >$10B off-balance-sheet/multi-year AV commitments).

Chapter 5 treated Uber One (>50M members) and dynamic pricing as frictionless compounding levers without quantifying how FTC ROSCA cancellation remedies (23-screen maze lawsuit) and the Oct 2026 FTC algorithmic pricing sweep could increase subscription churn or constrain surge/upfront take-rate optimization, nor incorporating CFO Balaji Krishnamurthy's Q3 2026 call guidance (~50% FCF buyback policy and Q4 $1.5B UK VAT FCF hit).

Separately, Uber's Delivery Hero tender offer secured 66.56% acceptance in Nov 2026 (additional acceptance through Nov 24; H2 2027 close) while an Uber loan backing SSW Partners' 14-market carve-out triggered EC (DG COMP), Korea FTC (KFTC), and MENA antitrust scrutiny.

Original Ch 3 omitted the December 2, 2026 EU Platform Work Directive (Directive (EU) 2024/2831) transposition deadline (rebuttable presumption of employment + mandatory human oversight of algorithmic dispatch/deactivations), understated the Nov 4, 2026 High Court of Australia 6–1 payroll tax loss (~AUD $81M NSW assessment, >AUD $100M multi-state exposure), and under-analyzed the FTC + 21-state federal ROSCA lawsuit targeting Uber One's enrollment/23-screen cancellation maze plus the Oct 2026 FTC algorithmic pricing inquiry.

Chapter 6 and Chapter 5 book/audiobook narratives retained stale FY2025 balance-sheet and buyback figures ($7.1B cash, $10.52B LT debt, <0.5x net leverage, >3x buybacks/SBC, 'never has to pause buybacks') that contradicted Q3 2026 10-Q reality ($15,664M LT debt up +49%, $10,068M unrestricted cash separate from $11,372M restricted insurance collateral, 2.65x 9M buybacks/SBC, ~$1.5B Q4 2026 UK VAT FCF headwind flagged by CFO Balaji Krishnamurthy, Uber-backed SSW Partners carve-out loan, and >$10B off-balance-sheet/multi-year AV commitments).

Chapter 5 treated Uber One (>50M members) and dynamic pricing as frictionless compounding levers without quantifying how FTC ROSCA cancellation remedies (23-screen maze lawsuit) and the Oct 2026 FTC algorithmic pricing sweep could increase subscription churn or constrain surge/upfront take-rate optimization, nor incorporating CFO Balaji Krishnamurthy's Q3 2026 call guidance (~50% FCF buyback policy and Q4 $1.5B UK VAT FCF hit).
